papers.title: LatticeMind: A Validation-Gated Agentic Framework for Density Functional Theory Workflows
papers.abstract: First-principles calculations are rarely single solver calls: they are multistage workflows in which structures, settings, and saved densities must pass correctly between dependent stages. Language models can write a valid single input, but reliability collapses once stages are chained: a dropped dependency, wrong file handoff, or hallucinated keyword can invalidate results even when the solver runs, and such errors surface only after costly execution. We introduce LatticeMind, a validation-gated agentic framework that converts natural-language requests into executable, checkable density functional theory (DFT) projects. A workflow contract specifies required stages, files, and dependencies; deterministic validators inspect the project before any solver launch; failed checks trigger bounded repair; and reports remain traceable to project files. On a 44-case RESCU benchmark spanning total-energy, density-of-states, band-structure, magnetic, phonon workflows, three non-flagship LLM backends reproduced every reference value; 119 of 132 runs passed on the first validated plan and the rest after one repair cycle. Ablations identify the workflow contract and pre-execution validation as the principal reliability mechanisms; a conventional trial-and-repair baseline reaches 71% at twice the token cost per success. The same architecture reproduces every reference value on a 19-case VASP benchmark, demonstrating transfer across solvers. Beyond these task families, LatticeMind generated and validated the 23 inputs of a multistage study of Rh-induced electronic responses at a Rh$_6$/In$_x$Ga$_{1-x}$N photocatalyst interface. These results establish workflow contracts, deterministic validation, bounded repair, and traceable records as a practical foundation for reliable AI-assisted scientific computing, where preventable errors are caught before execution and the solver is never the first validator.
authors: Nathaniel M. Vegh, Yu Zhu, Rapha\"el J. Prentki, F\'elix Beaudoin, Shuaishuai Yuan, Hong Guo

papers.title: Minimal-length kinematics of coherent light and a proposed two-color vacuum chronoscopy
papers.abstract: The unification of quantum theory and general relativity suggests the existence of a minimal measurable length, leading to a generalized uncertainty principle (GUP) and an energy-dependent vacuum group velocity. Testing these effects with macroscopic objects typically encounters the ``soccer-ball problem,'' where applying Planck-scale deformations to the total momentum predicts observationally ruled-out velocity deviations. We adopt the QFT-natural prescription in which the GUP modifies single-mode commutators, and verify by explicit calculation that the macroscopic group velocity of a multimode coherent pulse reduces to the single-photon GUP velocity evaluated at the central wavelength, multiplied by the classical Gaussian-beam factor, with no dependence on the total pulse energy. The energy--momentum relation $E=pc$ itself is unmodified; the deformation enters through the velocity--momentum relation and is equivalent to a modified dispersion relation in the wave vector, with a quadratic coefficient that depends on which of the two variables is used. The soccer-ball problem $\,$---$\,$ which arises only when the GUP is applied to the center-of-mass momentum of a composite system $\,$---$\,$ is therefore absent for coherent light, and macroscopic petawatt pulses probe the same parameter space as single high-energy photons. Building on this framework, we propose a two-color vacuum chronoscopy experiment using a short-pulse petawatt laser and its high-harmonic generation. By systematically varying the macroscopic beam waist, our setup separates Planck-scale kinematic shifts from classical diffraction delays, establishing a controlled, source-independent terrestrial methodology whose sensitivity we assess against current astrophysical bounds and against the dominant waist-independent systematics that limit it, residual-gas dispersion and the harmonic birth-time offset.
authors: Zhi-Wei Wang, Saurya Das, Samuel L. Braunstein

papers.title: Aspects of Anomalies: Fermion Family Constraints, Gravitational Form Factors and Scattering Amplitudes
papers.abstract: Quantum anomalies play two complementary roles in quantum field theory: as consistency conditions that constrain the field content of a theory, and as dynamical effects encoded in the analytic structure of correlation functions. This thesis explores both. In the first part, we study the 331 model, in which gauge anomalies cancel across families rather than within each one. Combined with QCD asymptotic freedom, this fixes the number of fermion generations to three. We analyze the model's symmetry breaking, scalar and flavor sectors, and its TeV-scale Landau pole. We then study the collider phenomenology of its exotic quarks, showing that the pair production of heavy quarks decaying into doubly-charged vector bileptons gives a clean same-sign dimuon plus b-jets signature, observable at a 100 TeV collider but not at the LHC. Finally, we introduce the left-right symmetric 33311 extension, which preserves the family-number constraint and avoids proton decay. In the second part, we use conformal field theory in momentum space to study the chiral, gravitational and conformal anomalies. We construct a complete off-shell parametrization of the non-Abelian TJJ correlator in perturbative QCD, identifying the dilaton-like anomaly pole. For the AVV, ATT and TJJ vertices, we prove mass-independent anomaly sum rules for the spectral density, showing that the anomaly pole is not an asymptotic particle state. We apply the TJJ insertion to the pion gravitational form factors at large momentum transfer with Sudakov resummation: the anomaly feeds mainly into the D-term and the trace form factor, improving agreement with lattice QCD. Lastly, sewing two anomaly vertices through graviton exchange, we show that the trace anomaly activates a gauge-invariant scalar gravitational channel, giving a double-copy-like structure in photon and graviton scattering.
authors: Dario Melle

papers.title: Commutative Coarse-graining on the Sphere
papers.abstract: Filtering by spatial convolution underlies coarse-graining and Large Eddy Simulation, the analysis of multiscale dynamics, and data processing across the sciences. Yet, as commonly practiced on the sphere, it violates a basic consistency requirement: commutation with differential operators, which is necessary for deriving coarse-grained dynamics and preserving the physics across lengthscales. We discuss the root of the problem, which is intrinsic to the curved geometry rather than being a result of metric terms, coordinate system, or numerical grid. A recently proposed generalized spherical convolution is, for a given scalar kernel, the unique linear operator commuting with the radial projection, divergence, and curl. Any consistent linear operator, be it spectral truncation, wavelet transform, diffusion, Green's-function inversion, or a machine-learned convolution, necessarily takes this form. From a simulation of an unstable jet, we demonstrate commutation to within numerical round-off, whereas common filtering that ignores curvature produces significant spurious divergence where none exists and gradient errors comparable to the gradients themselves.
authors: Chayut Teeraratkul, Hussein Aluie

papers.title: Concurrent Entanglement Purification Scheduling in Dynamic Quantum Networks
papers.abstract: Quantum networks must deliver end-to-end entanglement whose fidelity meets application requirements, which typically requires entanglement purification along multi-hop paths. Existing scheduling approaches either purify at the link level or optimize end-to-end fidelity for a static set of requests, and do not capture concurrent requests competing for network resources over time. This paper studies concurrent entanglement purification scheduling in a time-slotted quantum network with heterogeneous links, in which requests compete for link capacity and quantum memories, and each request may be served by multiple parallel paths for increased reliability. We formulate a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) scheduler that maximizes the number of scheduled requests, with max-min path allocation as a fairness criterion, and develop reinforcement learning (RL) schedulers based on DQN, PPO, and SAC, whose rewards balance request success against Bell-pair consumption. Simulations under varying network load, topologies and target fidelity thresholds show that the RL schedulers achieve the highest success rates, improving on MILP by up to 6% and on Progressive Filling and Greedy heuristics by 16.5% and 19.5% respectively, at the cost of higher Bell pair consumption and the deferral of a small fraction of requests. MILP, in contrast, achieves the highest fairness and the lowest Bell pair consumption in most scenarios.
authors: Gongyu Ni, Lester Ho

papers.title: Symmetry and Quantum Interference in the Attosecond Domain
papers.abstract: In this review, we examine the interplay of symmetry and quantum interference in the attosecond domain primarily through one- and two-electron photoelectron momentum distributions. Using our own work, we discuss how tailored laser fields provide control over dynamical symmetries, and how quantum-orbit methods make it possible to connect the resulting momentum-space structures to specific ionisation, propagation, and rescattering pathways. Particular emphasis is placed on ultrafast photoelectron holography and nonsequential double ionisation through recollision excitation with subsequent ionisation, where several distinct forms of quantum interference can be identified and manipulated. We also discuss how target properties, including the binding potential, orbital symmetry and parity, modify this mapping. Finally, we consider emerging opportunities offered by non-classical states of light, for which photon statistics and quantum fluctuations provide additional degrees of freedom for controlling symmetry and strong-field electron dynamics.
authors: C. Figueira de Morisson Faria, S. Hashim, J. Rivera-Dean, T. Rook

papers.title: Floquet Instability of Photon-Axion Conversion
papers.abstract: The discovery of axions would provide evidence for physics beyond the Standard Model. In this work, we investigate axion-photon conversion in the presence of a background magnetic field with simultaneous spatial and temporal periodicity. By performing a Lorentz transformation, the coupled axion-photon system is mapped onto a time-periodic linear system that can be analyzed using Floquet theorem. We find unstable modes associated with resonant crossing between Floquet replicas. The resulting complex Floquet exponents lead to exponentially growing modes, which we identify as a Floquet instability. Then, we determine the parameter regions in which this instability appears in a perturbative analysis. We further show that the Floquet instability enhances the axion-field amplitude generated from an initial photon field. Our results demonstrate that spatiotemporally periodic magnetic backgrounds provide a distinct mechanism for modifying axion-photon conversion through Floquet instability.
authors: Yuuki Sugiyama, Kazushige Ueda

papers.title: Linear Structure, Convergence and Resurgence of Hydrodynamic Transseries
papers.abstract: We construct an exact formulation for the solution of Bjorken expanding relativistic viscous hydrodynamics with a constant relaxation time and derive its late time transseries structure. The two fundamental modes of the linear auxiliary equation separate the hydrodynamic contribution from the exponentially suppressed transient mode. We show that this single transient mode generates the entire hierarchy of nonperturbative sectors through nonlinear mode mixing, while its decay explains the loss of initial condition dependence and the emergence of late time hydrodynamic attractor behavior. The hydrodynamic gradient expansion is factorially divergent for generic values of the transport parameter but converges at the discrete values $a=N^2$, where the auxiliary asymptotic expansions terminate. We further determine the exact Stokes constant of the auxiliary linear equation and establish its relation to the logarithmic Borel singularity coefficient. The vanishing of the Stokes constant at these exceptional values establishes a direct connection between auxiliary series termination, hydrodynamic convergence, and Stokes decoupling between the hydrodynamic and the nonhydrodynamic transient sector.
authors: Qi Zhou, Enke Wang, Hui Zhang

papers.title: Polynomial Spectral Gap Estimates for Finitely Differentiable Quasi-Periodic Schr\"odinger Operators
papers.abstract: We prove polynomial upper bounds on spectral gaps of quasi-periodic Schr\"odinger operators with small $C^{k}$ potentials and Diophantine frequencies. For sufficiently large $k$, the decay exponent is $k-34\tau$, where $\tau$ is the Diophantine exponent. We construct examples with lower bounds along infinitely many gap labels, showing that the leading coefficient $1$ of $k$ is asymptotically optimal. The proof uses quantitative reducibility and the Moser-P\"oschel argument.
authors: Ao Cai, Yang Gao, Jiawei He

papers.title: An Algebraic Formulation of Thermality in Nested Rindler Wedges
papers.abstract: Padmanabhan and Kolekar had demonstrated the phenomenon of recursive thermality in two dimensional free field theories where the Rindler vacuum appears thermal to an observer accelerated with respect to the Rindler observer. We study the same construction at an algebraic level for conformal field theories. At each step, a parent wedge is conformally mapped to a reference Minkowski spacetime, where a new right Rindler wedge and its left sibling are selected. We illustrate that under the Bisognano--Wichmann property, thermality holds at every generation: the state associated with a parent wedge becomes a KMS state when restricted to its right child. Further, using the modular structure of the wedge and its causal sibling, we identify the sibling algebra with the modular commutant and derive the corresponding recursive modular flow explicitly.
authors: Waheed A. Dar, Prince A. Ganai, Nirmalya Kajuri

papers.title: Gravitational baryogenesis in asymptotically safe gravity
papers.abstract: Gravitational baryogenesis in asymptotically safe gravity is considered. Two baryogenesis interactions are explored and their effects on the baryon-to-entropy ratio are discussed during the radiation era. The model's parameters are constrained with the current observational data, indicating these constructions may provide viable explanations for the observed baryon asymmetry.
authors: Rong-Jia Yang

papers.title: Hypercomplex Method for Solving Nonlinear PDEs
papers.abstract: A hypercomplex method for constructing solutions of a class of nonlinear partial differential equations is developed. A family of two-dimensional commutative associative algebras is introduced in which the structural coefficients depend on a component of the monogenic function itself. A corresponding theory of monogenic functions is developed, and nonlinear analogues of the Cauchy-Riemann conditions are obtained. It is shown that the first component of a monogenic function satisfies a broad class of second-order nonlinear partial differential equations whose coefficients depend on the unknown function. A hodograph transformation is used to linearize the nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann system. As a result, the problem of constructing solutions of the nonlinear equations is reduced to solving a second-order linear partial differential equation with variable coefficients, followed by the inverse hodograph transformation. A local correspondence between solutions of the nonlinear Cauchy-Riemann system and solutions of the associated linear equation is established, yielding a constructive algorithm for generating solutions of the original nonlinear PDEs. Several examples are presented in which explicit and implicit solutions of nonlinear second-order PDEs are obtained by this method.
authors: Vitalii Shpakivskyi

papers.title: Nonlinear Response of Schwarzschild Black Holes at Arbitrary Perturbative Order
papers.abstract: We establish recursive integration-by-parts identities that symbolically reduce the inhomogeneous solutions of the Regge-Wheeler-Zerilli equation to a small set of master integrals, yielding the nonlinear response kernels of Schwarzschild black holes at arbitrary perturbative order. We further derive a closed ODE system that enables rapid, accurate, and stable numerical evaluation of these master integrals. To demonstrate our result, we compute quadratic, cubic, and quartic quasinormal-mode coupling coefficients as special cases of the response kernels.
authors: Jiaqi Chen, Yu-Cun Xie

papers.title: Parallel Omnidirectional Atom Rearrangement with Dynamic Holograms
papers.abstract: The ability to assemble and reconfigure individual atoms is central to performing quantum science using optical tweezer arrays. Here, we demonstrate parallel omnidirectional atom transport and rearrangement using dynamic holograms generated by a single kilohertz-rate spatial light modulator. By carefully characterizing survival and heating, we show that atoms remain confined even when successive holograms are commanded before the liquid crystal has settled, enabling significantly faster transport. To generate holograms in real time, we develop and implement a warm-start, weighted Gerchberg-Saxton algorithm that achieves performance comparable to neural-network methods without requiring any training. Combining these techniques, we assemble ytterbium atoms into a 2078-site kagome lattice with 99.0% mean filling. In addition, we demonstrate parallel transport between array layers, combining axial and transverse motion to reconfigure atoms in three dimensions. Our approach is readily adaptable to existing tweezer platforms and provides a method for large-scale SLM-based atom assembly as well as programmable three-dimensional control.
authors: Samuel A. Engel, Dewei Gong, Ziguang Lin, Lysander Christakis, Kang-Kuen Ni, Norman Y. Yao

papers.title: Nambu-Goldstone Bosons and Quantum Fisher Information
papers.abstract: The quantum Fisher matrix and geometric tensor are powerful tools for quantifying the nature of quantum systems. Unfortunately, the formalism needed to compute these quantities is opaque and has limited the development of physical intuition for their behavior, even in the ground state. For quantum systems with continuous symmetries, we know the ground state can be understood in a model-independent and intuitive way from the correlation functions of conserved currents and charges. In this paper, we demonstrate an equivalence between the quantum Fisher matrix associated with the ground states of systems with continuous symmetries and the Nambu-Goldstone. bosons produced by broken generators. We will show that the information metric defined by the Fisher matrix is the same as the Zamolodchikov metric that defines the coset space of the system. Next we show that the Uhlmann curvature associated with multi-parameter estimation is the same as the charge density matrix that defines the difference between type-A and type-B Nambu-Goldstone bosons. We demonstrate these connections in several examples and discuss the generalization to finite temperature.
authors: Eugene Chen, Daniel Green

papers.title: Scale-separated AdS vacua on Riemann-Flat Manifolds
papers.abstract: Supergravity compactifications supported by fluxes and Casimir energy offer a simple strategy to concoct explicit, controlled and isolated vacua with parametric scale separation and soft supersymmetry breaking. Exploiting the special properties of both the Casimir and flux potentials with respect to Laplacian operators in moduli space, we prove that the simplest such class of solutions, given by toroidal compactifications of eleven-dimensional supergravity threaded by any fluxes, always exhibit perturbative instabilities in the form of tachyonic modes below the BF bound. This no-go theorem applies to any toroidal supergravity compactification supported by $p$-form fluxes. We also study compactifications on more general Riemann-flat manifolds (RFM's). Concretely, we find a tachyon-free AdS$_4$ vacuum by compactifying M-Theory on a $T^7/\mathbb{Z}_2^3$. This constitutes the first ever example of a fully top-down, perturbatively stable, scale-separated AdS without localized sources.
authors: Miquel Aparici, Ivano Basile, Bruno Valeixo Bento, Miguel Montero

papers.title: A Natural Dark Matter-Dark Energy Interaction from Axion-Monopole Dynamics
papers.abstract: We propose a natural framework for interacting dark matter and dark energy based on axion-monopole dynamics in a dark gauge sector. Dark matter is composed of dark 't Hooft-Polyakov monopoles, while dark energy is an ultralight axion whose coupling to the dark gauge field induces an axion-dependent dyon mass through the Witten effect. This generates a direct dark matter-dark energy interaction. We show that generic models with a significant dark matter-dark energy coupling suffer from a naturalness problem: the Coleman-Weinberg potential induced by the interaction is typically much larger than the dark energy scale. In our model, the corrections arise from a monodromy tower of dyon states, allowing them to be exponentially suppressed. In the minimal setup, the interaction strength is predicted to be $\sim 0.1\%$, below the sensitivity of current observations. We discuss scenarios in which cosmological population of higher-charge dyons can enhance the interaction to the percent level, producing an apparent phantom dark energy equation of state. We further show that the parameter space of the axion-monopole model preferred by fitting the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) results can also naturally explain the cosmic birefringence with a small anomaly coefficient.
authors: Hengameh Bagherian, Matthew Reece, Lian-Tao Wang, Huangyu Xiao

papers.title: Boundary One-Point Functions in the Open XXZ Spin Chain with Generic Integrable Boundaries
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of computing observables beyond the spectrum in the open XXZ spin chain with the most generic integrable boundary conditions. For such boundaries, the residual u(1) symmetry is broken and the familiar Baxter TQ equation describing the spectrum becomes inhomogeneous, placing the model outside the realm of existing approaches to correlation functions and form factors. We show that the Functional Separation of Variables method, so far developed mainly for rational, (quasi-)periodic spin chains, is largely insensitive to these modifications, and works equally well for diagonal and generic boundaries. Using this method, we compute exact determinant expressions for a prototypical example of form factors in open-boundary systems, namely the longitudinal and transverse boundary-spin one-point functions in arbitrary Hamiltonian eigenstates at finite system size. No constraint relating the two boundary configurations and no reference state are required. We verify the resulting formulae against direct finite-volume diagonalisation.
authors: Till Bargheer, Tengis Batmunkh, Paul Ryan

papers.title: Bilocal flows and universality with field-dependent regulators
papers.abstract: Many functional renormalization group flows employ a regulator that depends on the fields, as in proper-time and spectrally adjusted flows and in background-independent formulations of gauge theories and quantum gravity. Such a regulator generates additional terms in the flow, and their omission may spoil universality. We introduce bilocal flows, in which the effective action depends on the field and on the cutoff kernel as independent variables. The construction identifies the additional terms, and an exact sum rule shows that the first nontrivial coefficient of the anomalous dimension coincides with that of a fixed-regulator flow for every admissible regulator profile, so that universality is restored. For massless $\lambda\phi^4$ theory with a proper-time regulator, the reduced flow gives a profile-dependent anomalous dimension, while the completed flow gives the universal two-loop coefficient $C_\eta=1/6$ for every profile.
authors: Alfio M. Bonanno, Renata Ferrero

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Classical Simulation of BosonSampling under Any Constant-Fraction Photon Loss
papers.abstract: Understanding how photon loss changes the classical complexity of BosonSampling is central to assessing the robustness of near-term photonic quantum advantage. In this work, we present a polynomial-time classical simulation algorithm for lossy BosonSampling that applies whenever a constant fraction of the input photons survives. We consider the standard fixed-loss model, where $N$ input photons propagate through an $M$-mode interferometer and exactly $N-n$ photons are lost uniformly at random, leaving $n$ surviving photons at the output. For any constant surviving fraction $n/N\in(0,1)$, the algorithm samples from a distribution within total variation distance $\varepsilon$ of the fixed-loss BosonSampling distribution with probability at least $1-\delta$ over Haar-random interferometers, in time $\operatorname{poly}(M,N,\varepsilon^{-1},\delta^{-1})$. We further extend the fixed-loss analysis to the uniform-transmission-loss model and obtain analogous polynomial-time simulability for any fixed transmission rate $\eta\in(0,1)$. These results substantially extend the known provably simulable regime of $n=O(\sqrt{\varepsilon N})$ surviving photons or $\eta=O(\sqrt{\varepsilon/N})$ transmission rate, and demonstrate that even the experimentally relevant linear-survival regime can admit efficient classical simulation under the conditions considered here.
authors: Byeongseon Go, Hyunseok Jeong

papers.title: Cavity models of non-Abelian gauge theories
papers.abstract: In quantum optics and related fields, cavity quantum electrodynamics provides a powerful framework for modeling the low-energy properties of bound charges coupled to electromagnetic fields, using a minimal set of atomic levels and isolated photonic modes. Here, we develop a similar framework for non-Abelian gauge theories, focusing on the pure-gauge dynamics of SU(2) fields as the conceptually simplest example. Starting from the corresponding Yang-Mills Lagrangian, we derive an SU(2) cavity Hamiltonian in the Coulomb gauge, represented in terms of only three localized bosonic modes. Unlike its non-interacting electromagnetic counterpart, this model exhibits a nontrivial excitation spectrum featuring bound composite gauge particles ('glueballs') as the lowest-energy configurations. We extend this framework to one-dimensional arrays of coupled SU(2) cavities and discuss the driven excitation of a glueball condensate and the clustering of multi-glueball states as two elementary interaction-induced processes in these models. These examples offer a glimpse into the multitude of novel many-body phenomena that arise within this cavity SU(2) framework and we show how this physics at the interface between particle physics and quantum optics can be experimentally explored using state-of-the-art superconducting quantum circuits.
authors: Lucia Valor, Jacquelin Luneau, Klaus Liegener, Stefan Filipp, Peter Rabl

papers.title: Deconfinement on $\mathbb{Z}_{F}$ and Axion Domain Walls
papers.abstract: We investigate the nontrivial dynamics on $\mathbb{Z}_{F}$ domain walls and compute their tension in quantum chromodynamics (QCD) compactified on a circle with $N$ colors and $F < N$ massless fundamental flavors. In the process, we obtain insights on the $\eta'$ meson's potential in a regime where it is heavy and comparable in mass to other QCD resonances, as in Nature. We employ a center-stabilized compactification of QCD on a small circle of size $L$ with color-flavor twisted boundary conditions for the quarks. We demonstrate that probe particles in color representations of $N$-ality $N/\mathrm{gcd}(N,F)$ are deconfined on the $\mathbb{Z}_{F}$ domain walls whenever $N$ and $F$ are not coprime. This is reminiscent of deconfinement on axion domain walls in pure Yang--Mills. Finally, in the double scaling limit $N\rightarrow \infty$ keeping $NL$ and $F$ fixed, the infrared spectrum spans an emergent dimension. We establish that the $\mathbb{Z}_{F}$ domain walls are dual to electrostatic charge distributions in this emergent dimension. This duality allows us to compute their tension analytically and find a different tension scaling at large-$N$ between $\mathbb{Z}_{F}$ domain walls in QCD and axion domain walls in pure Yang--Mills, in center-stabilized compactifications.
authors: Paolo Bilisco, Raffaele Tito D'Agnolo, Arthur Platschorre, Pablo Sesma

papers.title: Gravitational Path Integral and String Theory
papers.abstract: Gravitational path integral has had many applications in recent years. Using the example of supersymmetric index, which provides one of the most controlled tests of gravitational path integral, we argue that even in this controlled case, naive gravitational path integral cannot produce consistent results beyond low orders. However one can go further using stringy inputs, e.g. the choice of UV cut-off and the choice of correct path integration variable, without having to do full fledged string calculation. We also discuss to what extent we are led to string scale UV cut-off even if we begin with a supergravity theory without an a priori bias towards string theory. This is a review of mostly published results, but we clarify several details.
authors: Ashoke Sen

papers.title: Classical solitons in anti-self-dual Yang-Mills theory
papers.abstract: We study classical soliton solutions in split-signature anti-self-dual Yang-Mills theory. Using Zakharov's dressing method, we construct rational lump solitons, which are localised near two-dimensional surfaces, and wall solitons, which have codimension one. We further describe multi-phase solutions which have multiple walls meeting at trivalent junctions and form four-dimensional foam-like structures. Two-pole solutions describe soliton interactions and we find non-trivial colour-dressed phase shifts for wall interactions. We consider the four-dimensional analogue of Ward's lump scattering for the restricted kinematics of coincident poles and show that there are non-trivial interactions in the collinear limit. Finally, we show that the determinant of the soliton matrix provides a $\tau$-function which acts as a potential for gauge-invariant scalar quantities such as the Yang-Mills Lagrangian density.
authors: Tristan McLoughlin

papers.title: Flux Vacua, Asymptotic Periods, and Relatively Anosov Representations
papers.abstract: We develop a topological method to detect classical flux vacua of M-theory on Calabi-Yau fourfolds with a single complex structure modulus using only asymptotic period data and monodromy information. To this end, we express the index of the F-term of the flux superpotential as a winding number along the boundary of the universal cover of the complex structure moduli space. The index evaluates to a sum over zeros and poles of a suitably normalized boundary F-term, where local contributions can be computed algebraically on a dense set of boundary points. Assuming a conjectured bound on the remaining contributions, sufficiently many sign changes of the boundary F-term guarantee a flux vacuum in the interior. We illustrate the method on the mirror Fermat sextic with explicit examples and a systematic flux scan. A main technical ingredient in our construction is a continuity result for projective period maps: we prove that the non-holomorphic (3,1)-period map extends continuously to the boundary of the covering space if the monodromy representation is relatively Anosov. In general, this property does not hold for holomorphic (4,0)-periods.
authors: Paul Balavoine, Severin L\"ust

papers.title: R\'enyi multi-entropy of graph states and the $n -> 1$ limit
papers.abstract: R\'enyi multi-entropy extends the R\'enyi entropy to pure states of more than two parties. It is defined by a replica contraction at integer replica number $n$, and the multi-entropy is its $n\to1$ limit. In holography this limit is conjectured to compute the area of a minimal soap-film web in the bulk. Understanding multi-entropy for general states, however, is harder. Unlike the bipartite case, the replica contraction is not a moment of a density matrix, and the continuation to $n=1$ has to be found by other means. We study this problem for qubit graph states. We show that at every odd $n$ the contraction equals $2^{-k/2}$, where $k$ is a sum of ranks of matrices over a finite field, one row and one column per qubit. We define a class of graphs that we call collision-controlled, for which the rank sum is a polynomial in $n$. This class includes graphs without even cycles and all complete bipartite graphs. The natural polynomial $n \to 1$ continuation is a finite sum over partitions of the parties. While the R\'enyi multi-entropy is non-increasing under single-qubit Pauli measurements at every odd integer $n>1$, the continuation to $n=1$ is not. A $Z$ measurement on one qubit of an odd ring with $2r + 1 \geq 7$ qubits raises it from $(r+1)\log 2$ to $(2r-1) \log 2$. Thus the continuation is not an entanglement monotone.
authors: Sriram Akella, Abhijit Gadde

papers.title: IR extremality and UV softness in string bootstrap
papers.abstract: Whether string amplitudes can be characterized by extremality within the space of consistent S-matrices is an intriguing question. We address this question within the framework of positivity bootstrap. We compute positivity bounds by minimizing the $F^4$ Wilson coefficient while fixing subleading coefficients, and show that the Veneziano amplitude lies close to the boundary of the allowed region. However, this numerical proximity does not imply exact extremality, as demonstrated by explicit counterexamples. When additional KLT-motivated UV softness is imposed, the Veneziano amplitude is found to uniquely minimize the $F^4$ coefficient for $4\leq D\leq10$, connecting the extremality of the Veneziano amplitude to its stringy UV behavior and offering a new perspective on what makes string theory special.
authors: Shi-Lin Wan, Ji-Yang Wang, Shuang-Yong Zhou

papers.title: AdS$_2$ from Type IIA on weak G$_2$ manifolds
papers.abstract: We present and study supersymmetric warped ${\rm AdS}_2 \times {\rm M}_7 \times I$ solutions of Type IIA supergravity, where M$_7$ is a weak G$_2$ holonomy manifold. Locally, the solutions are characterized by a cubic polynomial. We distinguish two branches, Branch 1 and Branch 2, and analyze their global properties, taking flux quantization into account. At the endpoints of the interval $I$ they exhibit either OF1-plane or O8/D8 type of singularities with Branch 1 allowing also for a Spin(7) cone. In the case of zero Romans mass, Branch 1 uplifts to eleven dimensions to ${\rm AdS}_4 \times {\rm M}_7$ whereas Branch 2 uplifts to warped ${\rm AdS}_3 \times {\rm M}_7 \times I$ with OM2-plane type of singularities.
authors: Niall T. Macpherson, Achilleas Passias

papers.title: Mapping AdS$_4$ quantum gravity via the Bethe Ansatz formula
papers.abstract: The topologically twisted index of 3d ADHM theory can be written as a sum over solutions to the Bethe Ansatz Equations (BAEs) of the XXZ-type model constructed from quantum toroidal $\mathfrak{g}\mathfrak{l}_1$. Via a novel numerical algorithm, we solve for all $p(N)$ physical solutions at $N\leq 21$, where $p(N)$ denotes the number of integer partitions of $N$. Surveying these solutions, we find that in addition to the known "1-cut" solution dual to dyonic black holes, where the gauge holonomies are distributed along a single curve in the complex plane, there are "dressed" 1-cut solutions dual to combined configurations of the black hole and M2-branes, $m$-cut solutions dual to $\mathbb{Z}_m$ orbifolds of the black hole, a discrete family of solutions interpolating between the 1-cut and 3-cut solutions, together with other exotic solutions, at each value of $N$. The free energy of the interpolating solutions cannot be matched with the on-shell action of any known bulk solution. The $1,2,3$-cut solutions and interpolating solutions all have a well-defined large $N$ limit, and their leading order distribution of gauge holonomies can be computed analytically. Whenever possible, we fit the contributions of the solutions to the index to all orders in the $1/N$ expansion with high-precision numerics, and extract the leading non-perturbative correction. With exceptions, these are matched with the results of equivariant localization in the bulk, and the action of wrapped M2-branes respectively.
authors: Cheng Peng, Xuao Zhang, Ziruo Zhang

papers.title: A group theoretic calculation of multi-invariants of some stabilizer states
papers.abstract: We study multi-invariants---a multi-partite generalization of Renyi entropies---of simple stabilizer states, for an arbitrary replica symmetry group. We develop a group theoretic technique for evaluating such invariants, which operates on the replica group and involves counting intersections among its cosets. Our techniques streamline the calculations of multi-invariants for graph states with two GHZ-like nodes and for certain generalizations thereof. The methodology developed here is most suitable when the quantum state is simple but flexibility over the replica group is desired.
authors: Bartlomiej Czech, Yichen Feng, Jonathan Harper, Xin-Xiang Ju

papers.title: Broken isospectrality in inverted black hole potentials and the emergence of Efimov scaling
papers.abstract: Are the inverted Regge-Wheeler and Zerilli potentials arising in Mashhoon's bound-state approach to black-hole quasinormal modes isospectral? Extending previous numerical and analytical studies of the inverted Regge-Wheeler potential, we present the first direct computation of the bound-state spectrum of the inverted Zerilli potential. Although Chandrasekhar proved that the original potentials have identical quasinormal-mode spectra, we show that their inverted counterparts have distinct bound-state spectra. We also demonstrate that potential inversion destroys their first-order Darboux relation, used by Glampedakis et al. to provide a simpler proof of isospectrality. A continuous interpolation between the potentials reveals substantially larger energy shifts in the interior than at the endpoints, indicating cancellations that suppress the endpoint spectral splitting. Explaining this behavior requires second-order perturbative contributions, even towards the eikonal limit. Despite these differences, both spectra exhibit asymptotic geometric scaling characteristic of Efimov physics, first discovered in three-boson systems. This scaling also applies to other inverted potentials with the same leading tail, including the scalar-field case studied here. Beyond their theoretical implications, our results raise questions for recently developed methods that compute quasinormal modes with high precision from numerical bound states.
authors: Umer Shahzad, Sebastian H. V\"olkel

papers.title: Model and parameter-path dependence of charged Dirac quasi-bound spectra in Born--Infeld and Euler--Heisenberg-type geometries
papers.abstract: We study quasi-bound states of a charged massive Dirac field in the exact electrically charged Einstein--Born--Infeld (BI) geometry and in a leading-order Euler--Heisenberg-type (EH) approximation. The two descriptions agree in the weak-field limit. We compare families in which either the mass measured at infinity or the outer-horizon radius is held fixed, and examine several field charges and levels. We integrate the radial equations outward from the horizon and inward from large radius, then match the solutions. The resulting frequencies show that the effect of the nonlinear terms depends on both the electrodynamic theory and the chosen comparison. For the fundamental like-charge mode, the small change in its real frequency has opposite signs in the two theories when the mass is fixed, whereas it is upward in both when the horizon radius is fixed. The fundamental mode decays more slowly as the nonlinear term grows along either family. The narrowest level, however, decays more rapidly when the mass is fixed and more slowly when the horizon radius is fixed. The spectra of the two theories approach one another as the nonlinear term is reduced. We also follow several higher levels; their decay widths and their response depend on the state and on the family used for comparison. The nonlinear coefficient is used as an effective parameter and is not matched to the microscopic coupling in quantum electrodynamics (QED).
authors: Bekir Can L\"utf\"uo\u{g}lu

papers.title: Active isolation of transmon readout with a tunable inductive bridge
papers.abstract: Scalable superconducting quantum computation requires fast, high-fidelity readout. Currently, this is assisted through cryogenic amplification of the readout signal. In traditional dispersive readout schemes, the amplifiers that are used to provide high signal-to-noise ratio also generate thermal noise that can decohere the qubits, demanding additional ferrite-based isolators to suppress this noise. Here, we integrate a chip-scale microwave switch, the tunable inductive bridge, into the readout chain of a fixed-frequency transmon. Flux-pulsing the switch, such that it transmits only during the readout, did not make a discernable difference to qubit coherence, residual excited-state population, or readout fidelity metrics. By injecting broadband noise that mimics amplifier thermal photons, we show that the switch suppresses the resulting qubit dephasing by more than $30$~dB, consistent with its independently measured on-off ratio, establishing it as a potential chip-based integrated replacement for readout-chain isolators.
authors: Chunyang Ding, Chuyao Tong, Paul Varosy, Nikitha Jain, Ziyi Zhao, Eric I. Rosenthal, Konrad W. Lehnert, David I. Schuster

papers.title: Exact spectral integrability of a finite-channel random Schr\"odinger operator: from fermionization of the Dyson--Riccati gas to Kontsevich integral
papers.abstract: We solve exactly, for arbitrary finite channel number $N$, the Riccati dynamics of a quasi-one-dimensional random matrix Schr\"odinger operator with Hermitian white-noise potential in the $\beta=2$ unitary symmetry class. The associated Dyson--Riccati eigenvalue gas admits an exact free-fermion representation at any sample length $L$, which in the limit $L\to \infty$ expresses the density of states and the total Lyapunov growth rate exactly through a single Airy Hankel $\tau$-function providing multichannel generalization of $N=1$ Halperin--Thouless formulas. The $\tau-$function further admits an outgoing-contour Kontsevich matrix Airy integral representation. Its saddle-point and double-scaling analyses give, in a unified way, the finite-channel density Lifshitz tail, and the large-$N$ spectral edge. In particular, for $N\gg 1$ the sharp $N=\infty$ edge is softened within an $N^{-4/5}$ spectral window, with its profile governed by the tritronqu\'ee solution of Painlev\'e I. We conjecture universality of this quasi-one-dimensional scaling edge profile for a broad class of $\beta=2$ random band matrices.
authors: Yan V. Fyodorov, Pierre Le Doussal

papers.title: Allight: A Perfect Photon Collector
papers.abstract: Collecting photons from quantum emitters remains a key limitation in light-matter interaction because conventional lenses collect light only from one direction. Here, we introduce a perfect light collector by inverse-designing a surrounding dielectric structure that encloses the emitter to increase photon-collection efficiency toward unity. Decomposing the device into several refractive interfaces enables emission collection from the full 4$\pi$ solid angle with adiabatic reshaping into a collimated beam. We experimentally demonstrate, in two dimensions, the ray bending that collimates omnidirectional emission. Our collector transforms current paradigms for highly efficient photon collection from narrowband, cavity-based techniques into experimentally robust, broadband, non-resonant dielectric devices.
authors: Dan Porat, Ran Finkelstein, Tal Carmon

papers.title: The next phase of quantum energy science: from mechanisms to applications
papers.abstract: A growing research community spanning quantum batteries, molecular and excitonic energy transport, polaritonics, quantum materials and nuclear control has begun to describe its work in terms of quantum energy or quantum energy science. What connects these otherwise disparate efforts is the deliberate use of quantum states, couplings, collective effects and engineered environments to control energetic states and pathways. A key difference from quantum information science is that the complete quantum state does not always need to be preserved; engineered dissipation or dephasing can even improve the desired outcome. We organize this emerging domain through a framework that connects mechanisms, functions, capabilities, and applications. We identify five elementary functions (Excite, Hold, Release, Transfer, and Transform) and examine the mechanisms that implement them. The same functions recur from the molecular to the nuclear scale, although their relative implementation difficulty can differ sharply. Moving toward technology, we highlight three engineering capabilities (Storage, Routing, and Conversion) through the performance metrics that matter for their applications. Stretch scenarios illustrate what performance targets could make these capabilities technologically consequential.
authors: Florian Metzler, Matt K. Lilley, Matthew C. DeCapua, Peter L. Hagelstein, Jonah F. Messinger, Nicola Galvanetto

papers.title: Central Limit Theorem for continuous $N$-particle systems in fixed- and high-temperature: single level
papers.abstract: We characterize central limit theorems for polynomial linear statistics of continuous $N$-particle systems on $\mathbb R$, in both the fixed-temperature regime $\theta=\beta/2>0$ and the high-temperature regime $N\theta\to\gamma>0$. In each regime, we give necessary and sufficient conditions in terms of the coefficients of the logarithmic Bessel generating function, together with an explicit combinatorial formula for the limiting covariance. At fixed temperature, this formula recovers the classical second-order free moment--cumulant relation, up to the factor $1/\theta$; at high temperature, it yields new second-order free $\gamma$-cumulants and their covariance relations. The proof combines moment extraction through Dunkl operators with a topological expansion of the logarithmic multivariate Bessel function indexed by ribbon graphs on surfaces. This expansion gives a topological interpretation of the free-cumulants: only genus zero contributes at fixed temperature, whereas arbitrarily high genera contribute at high temperature. As applications, we prove that $\beta$-addition preserves the CLT in both regimes and determine its limiting covariance from the input free cumulants, and establish a suitably rescaled transition from the high-temperature covariance to its fixed-temperature counterpart as $\gamma\to\infty$.
authors: Jiaming Xu

papers.title: Quantum Fluctuations and Wigner Dynamics of a Carbon Nanotube Oscillator Driven by an Atomic Force Microscope
papers.abstract: Suspended carbon nanotubes provide a useful platform for studying controlled nanomechanical motion in regimes where environmental fluctuations, memory effects, and quantum coherence can all influence the dynamics. We model the fundamental flexural mode of a carbon nanotube driven by an atomic force microscope as a harmonic quantum Brownian oscillator subject to a prescribed classical force and coupled linearly to a thermal environment. Starting from the generalized Langevin equation, we formulate the reduced dynamics directly in phase space, where the Wigner function evolves through a Gaussian propagator determined by dissipative linear transport, a deterministic force-induced displacement, and bath-induced fluctuations. For a Drude memory kernel, the retarded response is expressed through the three roots of a characteristic cubic equation. In the classical-noise limit, the three independent entries of the finite-time covariance matrix reduce to explicit finite sums over these response poles, eliminating numerical double-time covariance integration. We extend the construction to the full quantum fluctuation spectrum, obtaining a thermal frequency series representation that retains zero-point and low-temperature fluctuations. For an initial two-packet superposition, we examine interference attenuation and the integrated negative part of the Wigner function, which provides a phase space measure of nonclassicality. These results provide an explicit analytical framework for finite-memory quantum Brownian motion of bound oscillators and a tractable phase space description of driven carbon nanotube dynamics relevant to future quantum state preparation and quantum tomography experiments.
authors: Conrad Silio, Cristian Staii

papers.title: Large Deviations in Stochastic Dynamics: A Hamiltonian Perspective
papers.abstract: These lecture notes present an introduction to large deviations in stochastic dynamical systems, adapted from a lecture series given at the Les Houches school ``Large Deviations: Theory and Applications'' in July 2024. The exposition develops the theory through a unified methodology: WKB analysis of backward Kolmogorov equations, which reveals the Hamiltonian structure underlying all large deviation principles considered here. We treat three asymptotic regimes systematically. First, the small-noise limit for stochastic differential equations and the large-volume limit for Markov jump processes, where the Large Deviation Principle emerges from the Law of Large Numbers through progressively finer characterizations of fluctuations. Second, the long-time limit combined with small noise, yielding the quasipotential formalism for metastability and transition rates in both equilibrium and nonequlibrium systems. Third, the long-time limit at finite noise, connecting to spectral methods via tilted generators and enabling reduction of multiscale systems.We survey computational approaches including minimum action methods, their geometric variants for quasipotential calculations, and neural network techniques. The Schl\"{o}gl model of chemical bistability serves as a running example, illustrating both scalar and spatially extended settings. Appendices provide self-contained background on stochastic calculus and Markov jump processes.
authors: Lorenzo Cirigliano, William D. Pi\~{n}eros, Anna Poggialini, Grant M. Rotskoff, Eric Vanden-Eijnden

papers.title: Minimality and stability of the ball for the charge-qubit energy
papers.abstract: We study the shape optimization problem introduced by Mazzoleni, Muratov, and Ruffini as a model for a superconducting charge qubit, in which the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of a set of prescribed volume competes with the Coulomb self-energy of the ground state. We prove that, for sufficiently small charge, the ball is the unique minimizer, and that the energy deficit of a volume-preserving and centered perturbation of the ball is comparable to the squared $H^{1/2}$ norm of the boundary graph, with constants independent of the charge. We also obtain the corresponding results for the quadratic Hartree--Ohta--Kawasaki model.
authors: Ihsan Topaloglu

papers.title: Comparative Optical Spectroscopy of Er$^{3+}$, Tm$^{3+}$, and Eu$^{3+}$ Molecular Complexes at Cryogenic Temperature
papers.abstract: Rare-earth molecular complexes are attracting increasing interest for quantum information applications because of their structural flexibility and chemical tunability. Here, we compare the cryogenic optical properties of Er$^{3+}$, Tm$^{3+}$, and Eu$^{3+}$ complexes in the same ligand environment. Optical spectroscopy shows differing behavior across the three systems: spectral hole burning is observed in the Eu$^{3+}$ complex, whereas no measurable hole is detected in the Er$^{3+}$ and Tm$^{3+}$ complexes. We measure laser-induced local heating and rethermalization in the Er$^{3+}$ and Tm$^{3+}$ powder-like samples, observing strong local heating and slow thermal relaxation in the cold-plate cryostat. The recovery occurs over several seconds and, for some Er$^{3+}$ excitation conditions, extends over tens of seconds. The comparison across the three ions nevertheless suggests that heating alone is unlikely to account for the full contrast. Rather, the different behaviors of Eu$^{3+}$, Tm$^{3+}$, and Er$^{3+}$ point to ion-dependent relaxation and decoherence processes associated with their electronic level structure and coupling to the molecular environment. Temperature-dependent linewidth and line-shift measurements are further consistent with phonon-mediated broadening through coupling to crystal-field levels.
authors: Farhad Rasekh, Sahil, Arsalan Mansourzadeh, Diogo Alves G\'alico, David Hunger, Muralee Murugesu, Daniel Oblak

papers.title: Local obstructions to trapped-region escape in modified gravity
papers.abstract: Energy conditions in modified gravity are commonly imposed on an ''effective'' stress tensor that mixes physical matter with additional gravitational degrees of freedom, obscuring which sector actually controls null focusing, horizon multiplicity, and the disappearance of trapped regions. We develop a geometry-first alternative in spherical symmetry. For a normalized pair of future-directed radial null vectors, twolongitudinal Ricci projections and one independent transverse Einstein projection obey exact area-weighted transport laws. These imply a trapping-persistence theorem: after a nondegenerate future-outer marginal sphere, a regular ingoing generator cannot exit the trapped region while the ingoing longitudinal and transverse convergence channels remain nonnegative. In metric $f(R)$ gravity, with $F\equiv df/dR>0$, we then construct an entropy-resolved hierarchy based on the local Wald-density variable $Fr^2$. In the longitudinal entropy-focusing law, the scalaron second derivative cancels exactly, leaving a nonpositive scalar-gradient square together with the physical matter projection; in the independent transverse entropy-transport law, all scalaron derivative terms cancel. Entropy trapping is consequently governed by the physical matter condition $T_{nn}\geq 0$ and an algebraic mixed threshold rather than by a fictitious effective fluid. The resulting hierarchy cleanly separates matter positivity, geometric focusing, marginal-surface recovery, and gravitational-entropy evolution, and identifies the precise local reversals required for regular inner horizons, throats, and trapped-to-antitrapped transitions.
authors: Francisco S. N. Lobo

papers.title: Controlling Optical Quantum Interference with Plasmonic Metasurfaces
papers.abstract: The ability to efficiently control optical quantum interference by the same device is a challenging task that promises to enable key operations in quantum information processing. Here, we tackle this problem by presenting a composite quantum plasmonic metasurface operating as an ultrathin non-unitary beamsplitter capable of achieving both single photon bosonic bunching and fermionic anti-bunching interference just by varying the incident photons frequency or changing the design dimensions. The presented metasurface combines a plasmonic grating corrugated by periodic nanoslits that can achieve extraordinary optical transmission with additional nanostripes on top forming nanocavities characterized by localized gap plasmon resonances. The photon-photon interactions are analyzed based on calculating the quantum coalescence metric which accurately portrays the obtained bunching or anti-bunching quantum interference. The presented quantum interference operation is applicable to both fundamental non-classical light interactions and in the design of more applied quantum optical logic gates used in quantum computing and communications.
authors: Lawrence M. Qin, Sky Semone, Matthew J. Brandsema, Christos Argyropoulos

papers.title: Realization of de Sitter spacetime in AdS/CFT
papers.abstract: We construct horizonless, everywhere-regular solitons containing a de~Sitter core inside an asymptotically anti--de~Sitter spacetime, using an ordinary action of Einstein gravity, a Maxwell field, and a charged scalar. The object is a gravitating gauged $Q$-ball whose false-vacuum interior acts as a positive effective cosmological constant, sourcing an inner de~Sitter region joined through a thin wall to a charged, asymptotically AdS exterior. Two general requirements are emphasized: the scalar must lie in a near-false-vacuum (slow-roll--like) regime, and the exterior is driven to the extremal Reissner--Nordstr\"om--AdS locus in the thin-wall limit, in which the wall approaches the common would-be horizon. Since the solution is static and spherically symmetric, it may correspond to a semiclassical charge-$Q$ state of the dual CFT, realizing de~Sitter space approximately within a holographic theory. We also discuss free fluctuations whose de~Sitter--core modes appear as parametrically low-lying excitations above the state, bulk reconstruction, and the near-extremal regime, where finite-${\mathcal N}$ effects are expected to cut off the formal classical throat and replace its independent free-field modes by an interacting near-throat sector.
authors: Yasutaka Koga, Keiju Murata, Seiji Terashima

papers.title: Optimal four-copy detection of the three-tangle and its fault-tolerant cost
papers.abstract: The three-tangle, $\tau_3$, is a measure of genuine tripartite entanglement that distinguishes GHZ-type from W-type entanglement in pure three-qubit states. Here, we identify the statistically optimal one-sided four-copy detector of the three-tangle and study its implementation cost. The optimal detector has click probability $\tau_3^2/48$, while previous four-copy constructions achieve $\tau_3^2/256$ and therefore require asymptotically $16/3$ times as many experimental repetitions. Using the representation-theoretic structure of the problem, we construct an ancilla-free implementation of the optimal detector using 15 CNOT gates, together with an 11-CNOT detector with click probability $\tau_3^2/96$. These results reveal a tradeoff between statistical efficiency and implementation cost, since reducing the number of repetitions requires increasingly expensive circuits. We then show that this tradeoff persists once the circuits are encoded. In a fully fault-tolerant setting, the increased click probability comes with a substantial non-Clifford synthesis cost, while an early fault-tolerant implementation based on $T$ gates and STAR rotations reduces this overhead at the expense of additional encoded resources. We quantify these costs using both the Steane and $[[8,3,2]]$ codes, providing explicit resource estimates for implementing the optimal detector across different computational regimes.
authors: Federico Tom\'as B. P\'erez, Berta Casas, I-Chi Chen, Su Yeon Chang, Philipp Schleich, M. Cerezo

papers.title: From Hermite Chaos to an Attractive Log-Gas: Explicit High-Rank Limits of Iterated-Logarithm and Tail Constants
papers.abstract: Let $Z$ be a standard Hermite process of order $m\ge2$ and Hurst index $H\in(1/2,1)$. For $d<H-1/2$, let $Y$ be the variance-normalized version of the weighted integral $\int_0^1 x^{-d}\,\mathrm dZ(x)$. Its right tail satisfies $ \log\Pr\{Y>t\}\sim -\frac12\left(\frac{t}{\Lambda_m}\right)^{2/m}, t\to\infty, $ where the positive constant $\Lambda_m$ admits an infinite-dimensional variational representation. The same constant governs the sharp law of the iterated logarithm for weighted sums of nonlinear functions of long-memory Gaussian sequences. A general closed-form evaluation at finite order is not known. As $m\to\infty$ with $H$ and $d$ fixed, the normalized constants $\sqrt{m!}\,\Lambda_m$ decrease to an explicit positive function of $H$ and $d$, with relative error $O(m^{-1})$. This function also gives a lower bound for the normalized constant at every finite order. An exact R\'enyi variational representation at each order yields, in the high-rank limit, the entropy--energy variational problem of an attractive logarithmic gas. The limiting free energy is evaluated through the Selberg integral and the Barnes $G$ function. For $d\le0$, convergence remains uniform up to the memory boundary $H=1/2$. After division by the square-root boundary factor $\sqrt{2H-1}$, the high-rank and boundary limits commute. Their common value is explicit; for constant weights it equals $2^{3/2}\pi^3G(1/2)^8=2^{11/6}\pi e\,\mathsf A^{-12}$, where $\mathsf A$ is the Glaisher--Kinkelin constant. The quadratic and cubic coefficients of the fixed-order expansion of the normalized constant as $H\uparrow1$ converge, as $m\to\infty$, to those of the explicit limiting function. Global finite-order bounds and a concentrating-weight limit complement the main result.
authors: Elina Moldavskaya

papers.title: Soft elasticity of soft shells
papers.abstract: Soft modes of a shell are one-parameter families of non-trivial deformations that preserve the elastic energy. We identify all soft modes of the soft shells described by the variational theory of put forward by Sonnet and Virga (2025). They are seen to be strictly connected with the Bonnet families, a special class of solutions to the problem posited by Bonnet, who asked whether there exist non-trivial isometries that preserve the mean curvature. Differential geometry deems as equivalent all surfaces in one and the same Bonnet family, but continuum mechanics is interested more specifically in soft deformation modes and the shapes they traverse, as they may describe ways to ignite fluctuations of soft shells that ideally require no energy to be activated. We give a general criterion for the existence of soft modes and a method to construct them based on a cascade of path integrations. We apply both criterion and method to some exemplary cases.
authors: Andre M. Sonnet, Epifanio G. Virga

papers.title: Analytical solution of electromagnetic heating in a stratified absorbing medium
papers.abstract: We consider the temperature evolution in a skin tissue when it is exposed to an electromagnetic wave. The heating is caused by the absorbed power as the electromagnetic wave attenuates inside the skin. In many applications, the characteristic depth of attenuation is small in comparison with the lateral size of the electromagnetic beam. Because of this separation of length scales, the lateral heat conduction is negligible at leading order. Previously, we studied electromagnetic heating in a skin of a single homogeneous layer. We derived the leading-term analytical solution and the asymptotic corrections up to the second order for lateral heat conduction and for oblique incidence. In this study, we derive the analytical solution in the case of perpendicular incidence on a stratified skin tissue with a layer-specific profile for electromagnetic attenuation. It should be emphasized that in the current study, the heat capacity and conductivity are still uniform over the entire skin tissue; only the electromagnetic attenuation is stratified resulting in a layer-specific heating profile.
authors: Ulises Jaime-Yepez, Hongyun Wang

papers.title: Counterexamples to the total-current Hohenberg-Kohn conjecture
papers.abstract: The total-current Hohenberg-Kohn conjecture asserts that the ground-state particle density and total current determine the scalar potential up to an additive constant and the vector potential up to a gauge transformation. We give three counterexamples for two spinless fermions in the physically relevant setting of three spatial dimensions. In each, a Hamiltonian $H^{v,\mathbf{A}}$ has a nondegenerate ground state with identically zero total current but nonzero magnetic field. Complex conjugation then yields a second Hamiltonian $H^{v,-\mathbf{A}}$, with the same scalar potential and interaction, whose ground state has the same density and the same zero current, while the magnetic field is reversed. The first two examples are noninteracting. One is explicit, with a smooth bounded vector potential and a Gaussian density. The other has smooth bounded scalar and vector potentials in the standard potential spaces. The third example has Coulomb repulsion with unit coupling, an isotropic harmonic scalar potential, and Dirac monopole fields of magnetic charge $\pm 1/2$. The monopole example uses vector potentials defined on separate spatial patches, since these fields are not curls of globally defined smooth vector potentials.
authors: Andre Laestadius, Mih\'aly A. Csirik

papers.title: Double diffraction production for dipole-dipole scattering at high energies
papers.abstract: This paper is a first attempt to describe double diffractive production in dipole-dipole scattering within high energy QCD. Our approach is based on summing large BFKL Pomeron loops, which generate two clusters of hadrons separated by a rapidity gap. Unlike in the BK framework, our approach allows both clusters to carry large masses. We derive the cross section for the production of two such clusters and show that it exhibits geometric scaling. Testing this scaling behaviour against data from high-energy colliders such as the LHC will be a crucial step in establishing whether large Pomeron loops play a major role in high energy QCD dynamics, and in particular in the unitarization of the scattering amplitude.
authors: Carlos Contreras (UTFSM), Jose Garrido (UTFSM), Eugene Levin (Tel Aviv U.)

papers.title: Quantum-Seeded Distributed Post-Quantum Group Signatures for 5G V2X Communications
papers.abstract: Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) communications rely on elliptic-curve signatures that a quantum adversary breaks and on pseudonym certificates whose anonymity rests on rotation rate, not cryptography. This work presents qDGSP, a post-quantum V2X infrastructure: a hash-based dynamic group signature scheme (DGSP, over SPHINCS+ and WOTS+) distributed between a central controller and roadside verifiers. Group keys derive deterministically from quantum key distribution (QKD) seeds served over the ETSI GS QKD 014 interface, so no group-signature secret crosses the classical channel. qDGSP-EA (Ephemeral Association) binds an ephemeral ML-DSA-65 key to one group signature per 5G cell: messages remain unlinkable across cells, linkable within one. On a testbed with emulated 5G links, median end-to-end latency stayed within the 100ms ETSI budget for every variant. The qDGSP-EA intra-cell DENM matched the NIST ML-DSA-65 baseline on the wire, and under load EA mode raised delivery from roughly 78% to 93%.
authors: P. Blanco-Casal, P. Rejo-Iglesias, D. Cajaraville-Aboy, J. Vecino-Pe\~nas, R. P. D\'iaz-Redondo, A. Fern\'andez-Vilas, M. Fern\'andez Veiga

papers.title: Classical and Stochastic Trans-Planckian Censorship
papers.abstract: The trans-Planckian censorship conjecture (TCC) limits inflation to a deadline of $N_{\rm TCC}=\ln(M_{\rm Pl}/H_{\rm end})$ e-folds. We formulate it in stochastic inflation as a bound at confidence $1-\delta$ on the probability that a history outlasts the deadline, with three readings: one worldline, the region grown from one Hubble patch, and the reheated volume. Each reading becomes a closed-form condition, rigorous for a linear roll in leading-order stochastic inflation (for the region, in a branching model) and sharp at leading order in $N_{\rm TCC}$: a linear roll whose classical history lasts $N_{\rm cl}$ e-folds respects the TCC if $1-N_{\rm cl}/N_{\rm TCC}\geq\{2\mathcal{P}_\zeta[w+\ln(1/\delta)/N_{\rm TCC}]\}^{1/2}$, with $w=0$ for a worldline and $w=3$ for a region. On a linear slope without vacuum decay, the worldline and region readings are never weaker than the classical TCC, and on the CMB-normalized attractor all readings agree closely with it, so the bounds on the scale of inflation stand. A classical phase that ends in a flat quantum well, which the overdamped classical TCC excludes, is allowed with a margin of a few e-folds per worldline. Near the onset of eternal inflation, the readings differ. On a linear slope, a region must leave the fraction $\sqrt{6\mathcal{P}_\zeta}$ of the deadline unused at leading order: eternal inflation is excluded for every classical history that uses a finite fraction of the deadline, as is a band of non-eternal slopes, and the slope bound becomes $|V'|>V^{3/2}/[\sqrt2\,\pi(1-N_{\rm cl}/N_{\rm TCC})]$. Per worldline, every slope is allowed, given a margin of a few standard deviations. A false vacuum must decay at about the eternal threshold $\Gamma=9H^4/(4\pi)$ or faster for a region or the volume, but only faster than $3H^4\ln(1/\delta)/(4\pi N_{\rm TCC})$ per worldline. Whether the TCC forbids eternal inflation depends on the reading.
authors: Omer Guleryuz

papers.title: Orchestrating Key Scarcity: Global Capacity Allocation in Hybrid QKD-PQC Networks
papers.abstract: This article presents a Distributed Key Management System (DKMS) that provisions quantum-safe symmetric encryption keys to applications across a network. To overcome the distance and rate limitations inherent to Quantum Key Distribution (QKD), the architecture adopts a hybrid design: it utilizes multi-hop trusted relays for physical key transport, while applying an end-to-end Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) layer to ensure the relayed key material remains strictly protected from intermediate nodes. Because QKD transforms key generation into a scarce physical resource, managing unpredictable application demands poses a critical capacity allocation problem. The core contribution of this work is an SDN-driven control plane that globally orchestrates the network. Rather than relying on vulnerable hop-by-hop capacity reservations, a central controller simultaneously computes optimal filling rates and multipath routing for all per-peer key buffers. This global orchestration ensures that no application is starved and that all key buffers synchronize their filling processes. Evaluated on a Kubernetes-based digital twin across five distinct network topologies, the controller successfully filled all key buffers to capacity in under six minutes. Furthermore, under deliberately excessive demand, the network demonstrated graceful degradation, safely rejecting excess requests through controlled rate-limiting rather than experiencing catastrophic failure.
authors: Pablo P. Rejo, Manuel Fern\'andez-Veiga, Ana Fern\'andez-Vilas, Diego Cajaraville-Aboy, Javier Vecino-Pe\~nas, Rebeca P. D\'iaz-Redondo

papers.title: Shot Allocation Strategies in Debugging Quantum Circuits
papers.abstract: Debugging quantum programs remains challenging due to the nature of quantum measurement. As quantum algorithms and systems scale, it is increasingly crucial to develop rigorous debugging and verification approaches. Statistical assertion-based debugging validates quantum program behavior through repeated circuit execution and statistical hypothesis testing, but existing frameworks treat shot count as a fixed input parameter, leaving the problem of optimal shot allocation across multiple mid-circuit assertions unexplored. To improve debugging efficiency by making better use of given shot counts, this paper proposes and evaluates four shot allocation strategies within the QDB quantum debugger implemented within the CUDA-Q framework. These allocation approaches: equal split, static weight allocation, adaptive entropy routing, and sequential retirement, use statistical approaches to test whether qubits have expected state characteristics at different points in execution. We evaluate these allocation strategies on different circuits, under both noise-free and depolarizing noise conditions. We show how adaptive strategies use shots efficiently by concentrating them on assertions with high uncertainty. This substantially reduces total shot usage while maintaining comparable debugging confidence.
authors: Era Thaqi, Coco Gong, Margaret Martonosi

papers.title: Assignment maps for arbitrary reduced quantum dynamics
papers.abstract: Given an open quantum system $S$ with environment $E$, we establish a one-to-one correspondence between completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) maps from $S$ to $E$ and assignment maps initializing the composite system $SE$ in a possibly correlated state prior to unitary evolution. We show that every possible joint state $\rho_{SE}$ can be realized by such assignment maps, which are inherently Hermiticity-preserving and trace-preserving (HPTP). While these maps sacrifice global positivity, we derive a simple necessary and sufficient condition for any local state of $S$ to belong to their domain of validity. Furthermore, we prove that the geometry of this domain is governed by the joint state assigned to the maximally mixed input, ensuring that a non-zero volume of admissible local states can readily coexist with initial system-environment entanglement. Finally, we provide an operational protocol for witnessing such limits of validity.
authors: James Fullwood, Weixiang Ye

papers.title: Continuous and Differentiable Neural Network Representations of the Surfzone Sea-Surface from Lidar Point Clouds
papers.abstract: Ocean waves are often analyzed via sea-surface observations. Multi-beam scanning lidar enables two-dimensional measurements of the water surface $\eta(x,y)$ via sequenced point clouds of sea-surface elevation. Point cloud data, however, have to be gridded, interpolated, or mapped for use in wave analysis. We present and test a method for creating a continuous and differentiable (space and time), but grid-free, representation of the sea-surface from time sequenced lidar point clouds. We use a specific neural network architecture, a SIREN, to represent the sea-surface and to train the network on spatiotemporal 60~s of lidar data collected by a gas-electric UAS (drone) hovering over large (4 m), breaking waves in Monterey, California. The trained SIREN allows estimation of the sea-surface and its derivatives at any location and time. SIREN sea-surface representations tend to filter the highest wave number variability (splash-up and sea-spray). SIREN errors are comparable to instrument errors and insensitive to local data density. The reliability and reproducibility of our approach is tested by training two SIRENs independently on the same data. Differences between the two independent SIRENs are comparable to instrument error, but increase in data-poor regions. SIRENs' potential for directional wave analysis is demonstrated by computing spatial and temporal derivatives and by estimating wave velocity from a SIREN-generated space-time slice of the sea-surface.
authors: David R. Culver, Matthias Morzfeld, Falk Feddersen

papers.title: Two routes to the Hadamard condition
papers.abstract: In quantum field theory on curved spacetime, the Hadamard condition is often presented as a necessary condition on 'physically reasonable', 'vacuum-like' states of linear quantum fields, and plays a central role in many theoretical and foundational applications - ranging from proofs of the renormalizability of Wick polynomials to derivations of the Hawking temperature. In this paper, I strengthen, generalise, and bring under technical control two popular motivations for the Hadamard condition - one which appeals to the role of Hadamard states in defining physical quantities such as Wick polynomials and the expectation value of the stress-energy operator on general curved spacetime backgrounds, and one which appeals to the equivalence principle. This clarifies the role and status of the Hadamard condition, including its relationship to the equivalence principle, to well-definedness of physical quantities such as Wick polynomials and the expectation value of the stress-energy operator, and the sense in which Hadamard states are 'vacuum-like'.
authors: Eleanor March

papers.title: Quantum-Classical Hybrid Methods for Optimization: Lessons from Classical Decomposition
papers.abstract: Quantum and physics-inspired solvers provide specialized sampling interfaces for Ising and quadratic unconstrained binary optimization models, but constrained optimization requires broader coordination and certification. This survey uses classical decomposition to analyze how such solvers can be integrated into hybrid quantum-classical algorithms. We distinguish formal decomposition, reformulation and reduction, and computational orchestration. For each interface, we ask what the transformation preserves, which assumptions make the outer method converge, and which certificates the implemented inner routine supplies. The central questions are whether that information meets the classical algorithm's requirements and whether hybridization improves solution quality or total cost enough to justify its coordination overhead. Benders decomposition, column generation, graph reduction, and copositive methods illustrate this distinction by separating heuristic proposals from classical certification. We also distinguish component effects within a fixed wrapper, reduction--solver interactions, and comparisons between complete quantum-enabled and classical systems. The analyzed studies provide conditional component benefits and favorable co-design evidence, but do not establish transferable end-to-end superiority over strong classical comparators. The resulting framework identifies opportunities for constraint programming and operations research in structure-preserving design, safeguarded hybrid algorithms, and controlled benchmarking.
authors: David E. Bernal Neira

papers.title: Dynamics of thermalization in classical three-dimensional many-body systems: Non-Maxwellian distributions and the role of anisotropic trapping
papers.abstract: The physics of interacting baths is of interest in a variety of contexts, ranging from ultracold atoms to ionized gases. While many features can already be captured in a one-dimensional model, others are specific to the situation of two or three-dimensional systems. In this paper, we focus on three-dimensional features of a model for thermalization between two baths that we have explored in earlier publications. In contrast to the one-dimensional situation we show that, en route to thermalization, deviations from the Maxwell-Boltzmann energy distributions more akin to $\kappa$-distributions are observed. In three dimensions, these can be seen in changes at the peak of the distribution, which is precluded by the expected monotonic behavior of the energy distributions in one dimension. Furthermore, we consider thermalization for anisotropic trapping and explore its role in the onset of anomalous scaling with respect to the particle number. These results may be pertinent to the understanding of the interplay between turbulent behavior and nonlinearities for a variety of many-body classical systems.
authors: Roberto Onofrio, Bala Sundaram

papers.title: Generation of non-Maxwell-Boltzmann energy distributions during thermalization of interacting baths
